issues.legal_issue: An award was approved when the approval communication was read together with the request for approval and the parties’ subsequent conduct, so the original acquisition did not lapse.
material_facts: The Deputy Commissioner sent both the award in the prescribed form and the land acquisition estimate to the State Government for approval.
The State Government’s response expressly referred to the estimate but directed that the balance funds be made available for payment to landowners under the award.
The compensation amount was made available, paid to and received by the landowner, who then sought enhancement of that compensation.
The landowner handed over possession, which was subsequently handed over to the acquiring agency.
The State Government later asserted that the original award had been approved, while the landowner relied on later official letters to contend that it had not.
issues.conclusion: The award was approved by the State Government on 05.03.2010. The original acquisition did not lapse, and the compensation regime under the 2013 Act did not apply to the landowner’s claim.
issues.legal_principle: The approval communication must be construed with the preceding request and the subsequent conduct of the parties. The prescribed award form, the direction to make funds available for payment under the award, payment and receipt of compensation, a request for enhancement under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, and delivery of possession supported the finding of approval. Because the award was approved in 2010, the asserted lapse under Section 24 of the 2013 Act did not arise.

rule.if: land_acquisition_proceeding and award_and_estimate_submitted_for_approval and approval_response_directed_funds_for_award_payment and compensation_paid_and_received and claimant_sought_compensation_enhancement and possession_delivered

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The government initiated a proceeding to acquire land.
predicates.award_and_estimate_submitted_for_approva: The acquiring authority submitted both the proposed award and the acquisition estimate to the government for approval.
predicates.approval_response_directed_funds_for_awa: The government’s response directed that funds be made available to pay landowners under the award.
predicates.compensation_paid_and_received: Compensation under the proposed award was paid and received by the landowner.
predicates.claimant_sought_compensation_enhancement: The landowner sought reassessment or enhancement of the compensation awarded.
predicates.possession_delivered: The landowner handed over possession of the land to the acquiring authority or government.
predicates.original_award_was_approved_and_acquisit: The original award is treated as approved and the original acquisition is treated as not having lapsed.

issues.definition: When an acquisition proceeding has the stated approval request, response, payment, enhancement claim, and handover of possession, the rule treats the original award as approved and the acquisition as not lapsed.

issues.legal_issue: Land already acquired, vested in the State through taking possession, and paid for cannot be acquired again through later acquisition proceedings.
material_facts: The original award was approved, compensation was paid, and possession of the land was handed over to the government and then to the acquiring agency.
Later acquisition notifications and an award purported to cover the same land.
A project had been developed on the acquired land.
The High Court relied on later official letters to permit fresh acquisition proceedings concerning the land.
issues.conclusion: The later acquisition proceedings could not validly cover the already acquired land. The High Court’s orders were set aside and the appeals were allowed.
issues.legal_principle: Once possession is taken following acquisition, the land vests absolutely in the State and the former owner’s title ceases; the State cannot acquire its own land. The Court relied on D. Hanumanth SA v. State of Karnataka, State of Orissa v. Brundaban Sharma, Meher Rusi Dalal v. Union of India, Collector of Bombay v. Nusserwanji Rattanji Mistri, and Indore Development Authority v. Manoharlal. It also held that proceedings could not be reopened, including by re-notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, and that the asserted lapse under Section 24 did not arise after the original award was approved.

rule.if: land_acquisition_proceeding and original_award_approved and compensation_paid and possession_taken_by_state and later_acquisition_targets_same_land

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The government initiated a proceeding to acquire land.
predicates.original_award_approved: The award in the original acquisition proceeding was approved.
predicates.compensation_paid: Compensation under the original award was paid.
predicates.possession_taken_by_state: Possession of the land was taken by the government following the original acquisition.
predicates.later_acquisition_targets_same_land: A later acquisition proceeding purports to cover land already acquired in the original proceeding.
predicates.later_acquisition_of_already_vested_land: A later acquisition proceeding cannot validly acquire land that has already vested in the government through the original acquisition.

issues.definition: If an original acquisition proceeding resulted in an approved award, payment, and the government taking possession, a later proceeding targeting the same land cannot validly acquire it again.
